name: Gilead
overview: Gilead was a male member of the tribe of Gad, uniquely identified as the son of Michael according to 1 Chronicles 5:14. As a Gadite, he belonged to one of the twelve tribes of Israel. There are no additional notes provided about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Gilead means "perhaps monument of stones," reflecting a possible Hebrew origin. This proper name is not indicated to have been given by God, but it carries a geographical or memorial connotation as presented in 1 Chronicles 5:14.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Gilead was the son of Michael and infers that Jaroah was his father, both references found in 1 Chronicles 5:14. Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are detailed.
scriptureSignificance: Gilead's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Gad, highlighting the lineage of this tribe during the period recorded in 1 Chronicles. His identification as Michael's son situates him within the biblical record of Israel's tribal history, underscoring the importance of preserving genealogies for God's covenant people. Although not a prominent figure in narrative events, his mention contributes to the integrity and continuity of Israel's tribal heritage.
